paper_metadata.title: Hybrid Quantum-Classical Method for Bank Account Fraud Detection using Quantum Encoding and Quantum Machine Learning

summary: The paper evaluates an 8‑qubit angle‑encoded Quantum Support Vector Machine for bank-account fraud detection using 750 training samples from a synthetic dataset suite with over 1 million instances per variant. The quantum model underperforms a classical XGBoost baseline, which achieves roughly 89–95% ROC‑AUC, and the authors report no quantum advantage.

experiments.description: Hybrid quantum-classical fraud detection using a QSVM with angle encoding and an eight-qubit quantum kernel, compared against classical XGBoost on synthetic bank-account fraud datasets.

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Eight selected features were encoded, one feature per qubit, after preprocessing and scaling; categorical data was level-encoded.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Binary classification of bank-account fraud vs non-fraud using a quantum-kernel SVM.

problem_instance.description: Bank account fraud detection on synthetic temporal datasets from Feedzai Research with bias and missing-value structure.
problem_instance.dataset_name: Feedzai Research bank-account fraud dataset suite

dataset_specification.description: Six temporal variants spanning February to September; 31 features; induced Laplacian noise; missing values; group-size, prevalence, and temporal biases; 80/20 train-test split for classical model, quantum model sampled 750 instances (250 fraud, 500 non-fraud)

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Removed three columns with >25% missing values; removed rows with remaining missing data; removed duplicates; removed unnecessary information; level-encoded categorical data; scaled features; converted targets to numerical arrays and float types; reduced feature set from 16 to 8 qubits/features due to time and computational constraints.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Model run six times; evaluated using precision, recall, F1, ROC-AUC, accuracy/KPIs across dataset variants.

implementation_details.classical_solver: SVM with quantum kernel; XGBoost used as classical baseline
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Feature cleaning, missing-value handling, duplicate removal, categorical level encoding, scaling, train-test splitting, feature reduction to 8 dimensions for quantum model.

speedup_claims.conditions: Current hardware limitations; limited samples; quantum kernel reused across variants
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper reports that the quantum model underperformed the classical baseline and does not claim any speedup.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: unknown; paper provides no asymptotic complexity analysis or scaling study for QSVM kernel evaluation
limiting_factors: Quantum model trained on only 750 samples due to computational constraints
Feature count reduced from 16 to 8 qubits, limiting representation capacity
No complexity or scaling analysis demonstrating advantage
Classical XGBoost achieves ~89–95% ROC-AUC while quantum model underperforms

notes: The paper explicitly describes a QSVM with angle encoding and eight qubits, but does not name a specific quantum hardware device, provider, simulator, or circuit depth/gate counts.
Speedup order is not characterized asymptotically; the paper only reports empirical underperformance versus XGBoost under current hardware limitations.
Authors explicitly state the hybrid quantum approach does not outperform classical models under current hardware limitations.
Classical XGBoost baseline achieves ROC-AUC around 89–95%, while the quantum QSVM performs worse.
